claims.claim: Knowledge Base access requests are handled by a named team, GNS User Services, with a stated three-business-day turnaround; existing users add services through a 'Request Additional Services' button on the Knowledge Base home page, and Amex staff must log in from the corporate network.

claims.title: Knowledge Base | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also on the page: 'Locate the "Request Additional Services" button on the right side of the home page, and click it to apply.' and 'I am an American Express colleague /contractor? You must login using the American Express network'.

claims.claim: Inside Knowledge Base the interactive-guide copy describes search (including by document type), bookmarks, a profile page with recently visited documents, a Participant Directory reachable directly from Knowledge Base, and a Service Enrollment area for enrolling in GNS services in one place.

claims.title: Knowledge Base | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Guide text: 'Access to the Participant Directory is easy directly from Knowledge Base.' The directory's BIN / Card Number / Acquirer ID look-up was seen only in a search snippet, not on a fetched page.

claims.claim: Network policy for licensed issuers and acquirers is delivered as manuals (Business and Operational Policies, Network Specifications, Codes Reference Guide) published bi-annually in April and October and provided on signing an agreement; the BOP is explicitly confidential and existing participants are told to log in for policy details.

claims.title: American Express Global Network Policy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: FAQ on the page: 'The Business and Operational Policies (BOP) manual is a confidential document that contains sensitive proprietary information'. It also distinguishes the BOP from 'The Merchant Policy Manuals (Merchant Regulations, U.S. and Merchant Operating Manual, Canada)' which 'apply to merchants acquired directly by American Express'.

claims.claim: The partner bulletin is the Network Participant Updates (NPU), published on the second Friday of each month; it replaced the Network News and the Policy and Technical Release Announcement (PTRA) on October 12, 2018, and ad-hoc Special Bulletins cover issues immediately affecting issuers and acquirers.
claims.quote: The NPU is published on the second Friday of every month and provides Participants with policy, technical, and informational updates.
claims.title: American Express Global Network Policy
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page text: 'the Network News and Policy and Technical Release Announcement (PTRA) were retired and a new publication, the Network Participant Updates (NPU), was released' and 'As needed, Special Bulletins are published to address issues immediately impacting Issuers and Acquirers.' A December 2020 Online PIN FAQ on the same site cites 'Network Participant Update (NPU) dated April 2020: Dynamic Key Exchange (DKE) – Acquirer Enablement' and says 'Review future Network Participant Updates (NPU) for future announcements.' (https://network.americanexpress.com/globalnetwork/dam/jcr:c366753f-b040-42ce-8e0d-b7a8afa99323/Online%20PIN%20FAQ%20Dec%202020.pdf).

claims.claim: Partner Learning is the GNS training academy: an online essentials curriculum, live webinars with subject-matter experts plus on-demand replays, a six-module compliance course covering 50+ network policies, downloadable article series, and courses assigned according to the participant's Knowledge Base profile; registration is by email to PartnerLearning@aexp.com.
claims.quote: Customized learning tailored and assigned according to your Knowledge Base profile
claims.title: Partner Learning
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Tagline: 'Flexible, remote learning to effectively do business on the American Express Network.' The Backing Our Partners pages (/v4/partners/acquirers/backing-our-partners/ and /v4/partners/issuers/backing-our-partners/, identical copy) add 'Business Webinars' with senior executives, 'Training Webinars' on operations, chargebacks/disputes, policy and marketing, 'six modules that cover more than fifty Network policies', 'Downloadable article series to showcase our American Express expertise and best practices', and the PartnerLearning@aexp.com mailbox. Overview pages are public; course content sits behind Knowledge Base.

claims.claim: AMEX Enabled is the service-provider certification programme: providers register their company, enroll users, then work inside an AMEX Enabled Dashboard that includes a Messaging Center for document exchange and support from Amex product specialists.
claims.quote: Messaging Center helps Service Providers to upload and download documents, plus send and receive messages with experienced American Express Product Specialists.
claims.title: Partners | Service Providers | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Three steps on the page: Register Company (company details, accept agreements), Enroll as a User (access the AMEX Enabled Dashboard), Log into Dashboard. Product portfolios listed include SafeKey (3-D Secure), Click to Pay, Tokenization, Card Issuing, Mobile Issuing, Acquiring, Payment Platforms, Test Labs, Test Tools, QR Code, Integrated Payments Providers and Transit.

claims.claim: Amex claims more than 1200 registered AMEX Enabled service providers across 17 product portfolios and 45+ products; the June 2022 programme overview PDF gave 800+ providers with the same 17 portfolios and 45+ products.
claims.quote: join over 1200 Service Providers who have developed, certified and deployed their products and services for use on the American Express Network
claims.title: Partners | Service Providers | American Express
claims.label: Vendor

No outside check of either figure.

claims.claim: The June 2022 AMEX Enabled FAQ states there is no registration fee, names www.amexenabled.com as the entry point (it now 301-redirects to the Service Providers page), routes registration problems to AmexEnabled@aexp.com, and keeps the AMEX Enabled Brand Guidelines and press-release rules inside the Dashboard; user enrollment requires prior company registration with click-through NDA and Terms.

claims.claim: The Integrated Payments Providers Program is the AMEX Enabled track for POS software and service vendors serving Amex merchants; test cards, certification requests and questions route to a Payment Vendor Relations mailbox (mailto PaymentVendorRelations@aexp.com) rather than a ticketing portal.

claims.label: Verified

claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Segment landing pages for Acquirers, Issuers and Fintechs each carry Power of the Network / Marketing Solutions / Payment Solutions sub-pages; the acquirer page pitches merchant onboarding speed and closed-loop fraud tools, the fintech page custom product lines and data analytics, and each links only to Knowledge Base sign-in rather than any segment-specific portal.

claims.title: American Express Developers (client bundle index-CKDoS6PK.js)

claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: A separate, publicly readable Amex Payment Gateway developer documentation site (gateway-na.americanexpress.com) covers Hosted Checkout, Tokenization, 3-D Secure, Click to Pay, Batch and related REST-JSON/NVP APIs, with API version 100 current and a changelog; it is a merchant/integrator surface distinct from the Amex for Developers portal.

claims.label: Verified

Integration Guide pages are JS-rendered and returned only navigation text.

Merchant Reference Guide U.S. October 2021: POS device requirements 'available at www.americanexpress.com/merchantspecs, under Technical Mandates'. The merchant-login page is JS-rendered and returned no text.

'For a list of OptBlue participants, click or visit the website below: www.americanexpress.com/us/merchant/optblue.html'. Headline question: 'ARE YOU CLASSIFIED AS A PAYMENT FACILITATOR WITH LESS THAN $250MM IN ANNUAL AMERICAN EXPRESS CHARGE VOLUME?'

claims.claim: Marketing Corner (marketingcorner.americanexpress.com) is a public bulk signage order site for Merchant Service Providers ordering point-of-purchase signage for the merchants they serve, with a signage-team email link and an OptBlue cross-link; individual merchants are redirected to the merchant Signs & Supplies site.
claims.quote: This site is intended for Merchant Service Providers to order signage for the merchants you serve.
claims.title: American Express® Signage Bulk Order Form
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also on page: 'Learn More About OptBlue Help your merchants accept American Express with ease and speed' and 'Questions About Signage? Email the American Express Signage Team'. The merchant supplies site (americanexpress.com/en-us/business/merchant/supplies/) is JS-rendered and returned no text.

claims.claim: The direct-merchant Online Merchant Account (login /en-us/business/merchant/dashboard/, registration /en-us/business/merchant/registration) offers settlement and submission tracking, custom e-statements, online disputes, live chat and 24/7 requests; registration needs a Merchant Account Number, Access Code and banking information, with an 'I'll finish this later' limited-access mode, and enrolling in online disputes stops paper dispute letters.
claims.quote: Track settlements, submissions, and transaction information and customize financial e-statements
claims.title: American Express Merchant Services: Account Login | Amex US
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Home page: 'Create your Online Merchant Account in 3 steps', 'Submit requests any time and access live chat'. Registration guide (/us/merchant/support-center/registration/manage-account-online.html): 'Once you begin the sign-up process, you can choose "I'll finish this later" at any time to get limited access.' Disputes guide (/us/merchant/support-center/disputes/logging-in-and-enrolling.html): 'you will no longer receive Disputes letters in the mail. They will only appear in your Online Account.' A separate login host merchant-global.americanexpress.com/login is indexed.

claims.claim: The Merchant Website Support Center is a public help site organised by topic (registration and login, account, payments, disputes, fraud, data security, regulations, tax) with live chat Mon–Fri 8:00am–6:30pm ET after login, phone 1-800-528-5200 Mon–Fri 8:00am–8:00pm ET, and a 24/7 authorisation line 1-800-528-2121.
claims.quote: Quickly get the information you need to manage your Merchant Account, Payments, and Disputes with ease.
claims.title: Merchant Help & Support Center | Amex Merchant
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Header: 'American Express Merchant Website Support Center'. Article groups include 'Create new Merchant IDs', 'Edit bank information', 'Downloading reports', 'How to use the Disputes summary table'.

claims.claim: A distinct 'TPP' (third-party processor) merchant section exists for merchants acquired via processors: disputes there flow through the Merchant Services Provider rather than Amex's online merchant account, and Amex publishes a TPP-specific disputes reference guide; Business Class for Merchants is the public no-login content hub with no newsletter mechanism.
claims.quote: If your Merchant Services Provider asks for your help, you'll need to respond with the requested information within the timeframe they provide.
claims.title: Managing Disputes as Merchants | TPP | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page: 'In 2025, less than 0.030% of US Card Member transactions turned into disputes that reached merchants.' and links Amex-TPP-Disputes-Reference-Guide.pdf. Business Class for Merchants (/us/merchant/business-class-for-merchants.html): 'Explore tools, strategies, and resources to help reach and resonate with your customers.'

claims.claim: Bank of America's merchant help site, as an OptBlue participant, points its Amex-accepting merchants to Amex-hosted resources (Signage & Supplies, Shop Small Resource Hub, Disputes Learning Hub, Business Class for Merchants, Business Savings Suite) and to its own 24/7 line, not to any Amex portal.
claims.quote: access business resources such as signage and other tools and resource information from American Express
claims.title: American Express OptBlue Business Resources - Merchant Help
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Phone on page: 833.344.2324 'Available to assist you 24/7'. Illustrates that under OptBlue the acquirer, not Amex, is the merchant's servicing surface.

claims.claim: TabaPay's developer documentation onboards OptBlue merchants by email to TabaPay support, points to an 'American Express Network Requirements' page for data requirements, and still states the pre-April-2026 $1MM eligibility ceiling.
claims.quote: processing less than $1MM per year in American Express® transactions
claims.title: Processing American Express® OptBlue™ | TabaPay Developers
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Page: 'All major card brands in one settlement, in one schedule, in one statement.' Contradicts the $3MM figure on Amex's OptBlue page (see contradictions).

claims.claim: A payments consultancy frames the April 17, 2026 threshold move to $3M as tripling a merchant's runway before it must sign a direct Establishment Service Agreement with Amex, which brings its own underwriting and risk review, and says OptBlue pricing is consistently below Amex Direct pricing.
claims.quote: Effective April 17, 2026, that threshold jumped to three million dollars.
claims.title: Amex Just Tripled Your Runway Before You Need a Direct Agreement
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Page shows 'July 3' with an 'updated August 25' stamp and no year; no author byline. Quote on direct agreements: 'That relationship comes with its own underwriting, its own risk review, and its own set of hurdles.' Practitioner blog, not trade press.

claims.claim: In its FY2025 10-K Amex describes OptBlue as the programme through which merchant acquirers, processors and payment facilitators contract with small merchants and set their pricing, and lists OptBlue participants among partners that manage aspects of its customer relationships.
claims.quote: these third parties contract directly with small merchants for card acceptance on our network and determine merchant pricing
claims.title: American Express Company Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Also: 'Some of our partners manage certain aspects of our customer relationships, such as our OptBlue program participants.' Filing accession 0000004962-26-000080.

claims.claim: The 10-K describes the network partner base as third-party banks and institutions in approximately 110 countries and territories licensed to issue and/or acquire on the network, and never uses the label 'Global Network Services' or 'GNS' that the partner site's Knowledge Base uses; 'developer' and 'Amex Enabled' also do not appear.
claims.quote: These network partners are licensed to issue American Express-branded cards in their countries and/or serve as the merchant acquirer for local merchants on our network.
claims.title: American Express Company Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Text search of the filing: 'Global Network Services' 0 hits, 'GNS' 0, 'OptBlue' 4, 'network partners' 24, 'developer' 0, 'Amex Enabled' 0. Same paragraph: 'worldwide processed volume (spending on American Express cards issued by third parties as well as alternative payment solutions facilitated by American Express) was $227.2 billion' for 2025.

claims.claim: partnerportal.americanexpress.com, the only Amex property titled 'Partner Portal', is a Global Commercial Services referral portal for partners introducing commercial payment solutions, not a network or acquiring surface; it is login-gated and imposed mandatory authenticator-app MFA from November 1, 2025.
claims.quote: Work with American Express to introduce commercial payment solutions to your contacts.
claims.title: Partner Portal USA | American Express
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Banner: 'STARTING NOV 1, 2025, YOU WILL NEED TO USE AN AUTHENTICATOR MOBILE APP IN ADDITION TO PASSWORD TO ACCESS PARTNER PORTAL'. Registration form (/apex/registration?country=USA&lang=en-US&acttype=ba) asks for company, tax ID and sales rep; not submitted. Included so it is not mistaken for a network partner portal.

claims.claim: The named 'Amex Merchant Financing' product has no live surface: its US business-funding URL redirects to the Business Line of Credit page and merchantfinancing.americanexpress.com does not resolve in DNS.
claims.quote: American Express® Business Line of Credit offers line sizes from $2,000 to $250,000.
claims.title: Business Line of Credit | American Express US
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: curl followed a redirect to https://www.americanexpress.com/en-us/business/business-line-of-credit/; WebFetch of https://merchantfinancing.americanexpress.com/ returned 'getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND'. Third-party lender-review sites (search snippets, not fetched) state Amex is not taking new Merchant Financing applications.

claims.claim: A search-indexed copy of the GNS registration page on the QA host qnetwork.americanexpress.com describes Knowledge Base as the replacement for the earlier GNSweb extranet; the production /globalnetwork/register/ page redirects to the enterprise login and the QA host returned HTTP 503, so this could not be read on a live page.
claims.quote: replaces GNSweb to provide an enhanced interface for accessing all Global Network assets, applications and services
claims.title: Create an Account
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Several qnetwork.americanexpress.com pages (v4 home, sign-in, service-providers, amex-enabled enroll-user) are indexed by search engines; all fetch attempts returned 503 on 2026-09-25.
